claims.hypothesis: The CO-to-H2 X-factor in the Galactic bar is lower than the standard Galactic value
claims.experiment: Calibrate X-factor from 13CO LTE masses of bar clouds and estimate 12CO optical depth
claims.result: Average X-factor (1.59 +/- 0.5)e19 cm^-2 (K km/s)^-1 and low 12CO optical depth in bar clouds
claims.finding: X-factor in the bar is 10-20 times lower than the standard value, likely from low optical depth

evidence.quote: We also measure the CO-to-H~2~ X-factor in the bar to be an order of magnitude lower than the typical Galactic value.
indicates that the standard Galactic X-factor is an overestimate by 10-20 times in this region.

claims.hypothesis: Broad-line, warm NH3 clouds lie in the Galactic bar
claims.experiment: Select clouds by NH3 (1,1) width above 10 km/s and check with geometry, distances and derived properties
claims.result: Nine clouds are grouped as bar clouds; G350.18 and G350.10 reclassified; some clouds may be in the disk despite atypical properties
claims.finding: Nine clouds likely lie in the bar region with distance and location uncertain

evidence.quote: Although some clouds may be in the Galactic disk despite their atypical properties, nine clouds are likely associated with regions in the Galactic bar

why_this_data.value: Clouds picked for bright, large-scale NH3 (3,3) emission, implying warm gas, and often broad lines, suggesting a Galactic bar location; ACA observes several tracers of temperature, shocks, SF and turbulence

evidence.quote: The clouds were selected on the basis of bright, large-scale NH~3~ (3,3) emission, which is only observed toward a few objects
in order to probe physical parameters including temperature, shocks, ionization, star formation, and turbulence, and to investigate where these clouds are located.

limitations_admitted.value: Single-phase gas assumption is an oversimplification

referee_caveats_inferred: Bar membership rests mainly on NH3 line width above 10 km/s and assumed positions on the bar major axis, so the SF-suppression result partly depends on this selection (circularity)
The suppression claim relies on detection versus nondetection with no direct inverse Mach-SFR correlation
Only the TP data were used; the 7 m data and its possible resolution gain are ignored
H2CO temperatures assume 1e4 cm^-3, while the authors' own RADEX test finds no consistent density for most clouds
Mach numbers use H2CO temperatures yet ammonia temperature is the one correlating, so the thermal/turbulent interpretation could be affected by gas-phase mixing
The X-factor depends on 13CO LTE masses and Galactocentric isotope ratios with large coefficients' uncertainty (e.g. +/-82.6 intercept)
Calzetti and Murphy SFR calibrations are galaxy-scale and may not apply to single clouds
